title: Pin decision matrix and compatibility annotation protocol for unvetted open weights
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: define a lightweight, auditable decision matrix and a simple annotation protocol that clarify when newly submitted open model weights are pinned to a specific runtime/model variant, when they may remain unpinned (soft-entry), and how compatibility notes and runtime tags propagate through the catalog.

Context and motivation:
- We ingest a high volume of community/open models with varying degrees of provenance and testing. Current intake guidance is fragmented across PRDs and intake tickets; engineers and catalog reviewers make ad-hoc pinning choices which causes inconsistent runtime routing and surprise regressions for customers.
- The goal is to reduce ambiguity for catalog maintainers, enable automated routing rules, and create clear rollback/fallback semantics for unpinned entries. This must be operationalizable by Eng (runtime), Catalog UI (Console), and our onboarding reviewers.

Scope (in):
- Define decision matrix (criteria) that results in one of: PIN (hard pin to runtime variant), SOFT-ENTRY (unfrozen unpinned with metadata flags), or HOLD (needs more info).
- Define required compatibility annotations/fields to be present on intake: architecture fingerprint, quantization compatibility, KV-cache expectations, min_supported_sequence_length, known-fallback-variants, provenance score.
- Define propagation rules: how compatibility notes map to runtime tags (e.g., kernel-optimized, quant-4bit-safe) and how they influence routing & fallback.
- Acceptance criteria for minimally passing intake that allows staged canary serving.

Out of scope (future work): automated runtime compatibility probes (ENG will own), complex semantic safety gates, billing/price tier recommendations.

Success signals:
- Catalog reviewers show >80% adherence to decision matrix in a 2-week pilot.
- Reduction in post-ingest compatibility incidents attributed to mis-pinning by 50% in the first quarter after rollout.

Deliverables:
- Decision matrix spreadsheet with rules and examples (CSV/Drive link).
- Short PRD (this ticket + linked doc) describing the annotation schema and mapping rules.
- Acceptance criteria checklist to be wired into intake UI and reviewer workflow.
- Example intake records (3 example model entries) demonstrating PIN vs SOFT-ENTRY vs HOLD.
acceptance_criteria: Documented decision matrix with explicit threshold fields (provenance_score, eval_pass_rate, runtime_probe_status) that map to one of: PIN, SOFT-ENTRY, HOLD.

Compatibility annotation schema specified: list of required keys and allowed values (architecture, ops_compat, quant_profiles, fallback_variants, kv_cache_behavior, seq_length_bounds, provenance_url).
Mapping table from compatibility annotations to runtime tags (e.g., quant-4bit-safe -> quant-compat:true, kernel_group:A), with at least 5 canonical mappings recorded.
Reviewer checklist integrated into intake flow (Confluence link + template) and validated in two pilot intakes performed by the Onboarding squad.
Example metadata payloads for three model entries committed to the ingest test bucket demonstrating each outcome (PIN, SOFT-ENTRY, HOLD).
Console should be able to display the compatibility annotations and the effective pin status for any catalog entry (mockup + acceptance signoff from Design).
Security review completed (sec approves schema or records outstanding blockers) before wide rollout.
Telemetry hooks defined: events for "ingest_decision", "pin_change", and "compat_flag_mismatch" with suggested properties so ENG can implement probes.
Rollout notes: soft-entry models must default to a conservative routing policy (lower memory footprint, smaller batch sizes) until runtime probes are green.
notes: Provenance score is a normalized 0-100 integer calculated by intake heuristics (see PM-472819 for details).
We should prefer soft-entry where possible to enable discovery, but require a minimum eval_pass_rate (>70%) for HTTP serving to avoid frequent customer-facing regressions.
When PIN is chosen, include an explicit pin_reason string and the approving_reviewer. This will help audits and rollback decisions.
Compatibility annotations should be terse — aim for a 5-10 key payload that covers runtime-impacting attributes only.
Suggested telemetry properties: model_id, decision, provenance_score, eval_pass_rate, reviewer, timestamp, runtime_tags_applied.
Example fallback rule: if model's quant_profile == 'q4_approx' and runtime reports quant_incompatibility, route to fallback_variant tagged 'cpu-safe' and surface warning in console.
comments: 2025-02-13 — Marco Li: Drafted decision matrix stub and shared CSV with Eng & Design. Requesting review from runtime owners (ENG-2042) and Design for console affordance.
2025-02-18 — Priya Menon (Design): Mockups attached in the Confluence page. Recommend a collapsed 'compatibility' panel to avoid cluttering the catalog entry view.
2025-02-20 — Ravi Gupta (Security): Noted that provenance_url must be whitelisted and stored in audit logs. Flagged potential PII in model card metadata — recommend schema hygiene rules.

2025-02-24 — Eng runtime lead (Elena Kozlova): Agreed to implement telemetry events after schema is finalized. Raised a question about how strict 'min_supported_sequence_length' should be for backward compatibility — suggested 'soft-warning' semantics for mismatches.
2025-02-27 — Aisha Patel: Incorporated feedback; updated acceptance criteria to require security review and telemetry spec. Assigned eng dependency to ENG-2042 for probe adapters.
2025-03-01 — Marco Li: Ready for stakeholder review. Next steps: pilot with 4 community models next cycle, coordination with Onboarding reviewers for training.
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chose 3-tier outcome (PIN / SOFT-ENTRY / HOLD) over binary pin/unpin to balance discoverability and safety.

2025-02-17: Require provenance_score and at least one eval_pass_rate metric for soft-entry; explicit pin required for models with provenance_score < 40 but high eval scores (>=85%) — edge case to be handled by reviewer escalation.
2025-02-21: Compatibility annotations will be defined as a flat key-value map; nested compatibility schemas were rejected to keep ingestion simple.
2025-02-25: Telemetry contract agreed: ingestion decision events must include runtime_tag_list and reviewer if present.
